awaiting_james.detail: backend/solar.py line 13 sets SFI_URL to https://services.swpc.noaa.gov/json/solar-cycle/observed-solar-cycle-indices.json. That file is MONTHLY, not daily: its records are time-tagged year-month ("1749-01" onward) and each row is a monthly mean. So the sfi and ssn the whole site runs on are last month's averages, and they cannot change until the month rolls over. CONFIRMED FACTS: the URL is what solar.py reads (source read directly); the file is monthly (granularity read from the file); /api/health has reported sfi 116 on 2026-09-22, 09-23 and 09-30, and every recent /api/solar/history row carries the identical sfi 116, a_index 7, ssn 76 while its timestamp advances every 15 minutes; the site's own hamqsl feed, fetched through /api/feed tonight and updated 30 Sep 2026 0410 GMT, reports solarflux 92. So dxedge.net currently shows 116 on the dashboard and 92 on the cyber page, from the same origin, about 24 points apart. INFERENCE, not confirmed: that 116 is a September or August monthly mean and the gap will persist until the month turns. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND the number on screen: sfi is passed straight into the propagation model, backend/main.py feeds it to predict_path at lines 267, 296 and 375 and uses round(sfi) in the voacap and recommendation cache keys, so a 24-point overstatement biases every band recommendation optimistic and freezes the cache key for a month at a time. It also breaks two alerts in backend/alerts.py: the 10m opening alert fires on sfi >= 150 and the sfi_drop alert compares against prev_sfi, and neither can behave sensibly on a value that only moves once a month. Separately and more minor, a_index is not measured at all: line 58 derives it from a hardcoded Kp lookup table, so the displayed A index is a function of Kp rather than a real A index. NOT FIXED AUTONOMOUSLY, deliberately: swapping the endpoint changes what the number means, which is explicitly an escalation ("a feed replacement that changes data semantics"). DECISION NEEDED: should solar.py move to a daily 10.7cm source? awaiting_james.detail: Security-relevant, pre-existing, and not previously tracked. frontend/src/components/Support.jsx renders the donation QR codes as pointing at a third party: https://api.qrserver.com/v1/create-qr-code/?size=NxN&data=&bgcolor=0e0e0e&color=7affb2&qzone=2. The values passed in the data param are the page's BTC address (bc1q99...dgxl), ETH address (0x450Af...82db), https://paypal.me/sagejw and now https://ko-fi.com/oldtimeradio. CONCRETE RISK, and it is worse than the ordinary third-party-asset case: the QR is the artifact a visitor actually scans, and a compromised, hijacked or MITM'd api.qrserver.com could return a QR encoding a DIFFERENT wallet address while the plain-text address printed next to it stays correct. People scan QR codes without reading the address underneath, so donations would silently redirect with no visible tell and no integrity check available - an cannot carry subresource integrity, and the URL is built fresh on every render. Secondary issues: the addresses are disclosed to a third party on every page view (minor, they are public by design), and the QRs break if the service goes down. PROVENANCE, stated precisely so this is not misread as a regression: Support.jsx was added by James himself in 59111ba on 2026-05-31, and the 7 OTR commits of 2026-10-01 only changed its KOFI constant. The dependency is James's own and about four months old. It surfaced tonight only because reviewing those commits meant reading the file, and it appears in neither known_issues nor awaiting_james, so it has never been reported. NOT fixed autonomously: it is not link rot, not a redirect, not a deprecated feed endpoint and not an /api/feed bypass (an image load is not a CORS fetch and cannot go through a proxy that returns text, same reasoning as otr-audio-is-a-media-element-not-a-feed), so it falls outside all four repair categories. It is also closely analogous to crane-cab-third-party-cdn, which was escalated rather than fixed. OPTIONS: (a) leave as is; (b) generate the QR codes client-side from a vendored QR library, which removes the third party entirely and is the clean fix; (c) pre-generate the four QR PNGs once, eyeball-verify each decodes to the right address, and commit them as static assets, which also removes the runtime dependency and is the smallest change; (d) drop the QR codes and show copy-to-clipboard text addresses only. Recommend (c) for the crypto addresses specifically, since those are the ones where a swap costs real money and the address set almost never changes. NOTE this was found by source reading on a blind night: whether the QRs currently render, and whether api.qrserver.com is even reachable, was NOT verified.

awaiting_james.detail: CORRECTION, 2026-10-13 22:50 PT, from the interactive session that pushed 69a1385: this was a FALSE ALARM and the item is CLOSED. 69a1385's own deploy landed within about 2 minutes. Measured at 03:15-03:17 UTC, an hour BEFORE this run probed: WebFetch of https://dxedge.net/sw.js?v=69a1385 read CACHE_NAME 'dxedge-v69'; WebFetch of /synth/index.html?v=69a1385 read title 'Filament - a tube synthesizer - DXEdge'; a headless Chromium loaded https://dxedge.net/synth/, the engine came up and rendered audio, and the main page showed the Filament tab; curl -D of /synth/rack.js returned 'Cache-Control: no-cache, must-revalidate', i.e. nginx had already restarted onto 69a1385's /synth/ carve-out. LIKELY CAUSE of the stale reading (inference, not proven): the same session had fetched the BARE URLs /sw.js and /synth/ at about 03:14 UTC, seconds before the deploy finished, and those pre-deploy responses (v68, SPA catch-all) appear to have been served from a WebFetch cache to this later run. LESSON: always put a fresh cache-busting query on WebFetch deploy checks (the sw.js tripwire included); a bare URL can return another session's earlier copy. No Actions log needs reading. ORIGINAL TEXT FOLLOWS. Commit 69a1385 "feat(synth): Filament v0.1" (2026-10-12 20:14:04 PT) and 0e2c2c4 (20:16:55 PT) have not reached production, confirmed ~70 minutes later by two independent signals: production sw.js CACHE_NAME is dxedge-v68 while repo HEAD is dxedge-v69 (bumped by 69a1385 itself), and https://dxedge.net/synth/ serves the SPA catch-all with no "Filament" string, which is nginx behaviour when frontend/dist has no synth/ directory. At 70 minutes against a 6-10 minute deploy this is a failed or never-started workflow run. WHAT I CANNOT DO: read the cause. api.github.com is blocked by the sandbox egress proxy, so the Actions run status, the step that failed and the droplet deploy log are all unreadable from here, and there is no workflow_dispatch. WHY I DID NOT JUST FORCE IT: 69a1385 modifies nginx/nginx.conf, which the brief names as an escalate-only file, and that same nginx change is what sets backend=true in deploy.yml and selects the --no-cache rebuild branch, which is the likeliest place for the failure to live. Pushing blind retries at an infrastructure change I am not allowed to author is guessing. WHAT YOU NEED TO DO: open the Actions run for 69a1385 and read which step failed. Most likely candidates from reading deploy.yml are the Crane Cab stamp step (it is designed to fail the deploy rather than ship a build claiming to be dev), the frontend build, or the backend verify step that checks the container restarted. ONE IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this run pushed state.json, whose deploy has BEFORE=0e2c2c4 and therefore CHANGED=scripts/health/state.json alone, backend=false, frontend-only branch. That may land the synth frontend and bump sw.js to v69 while leaving the nginx /synth/ carve-out unapplied, so a working /synth/ tomorrow is NOT evidence the original deploy succeeded. Check the Actions history, not the symptom. UPDATE, SAME NIGHT, READ THIS BEFORE ACTING ON THE ABOVE. The gap is CLOSED and the caveat in the preceding paragraph was wrong. This routine's state.json push (115e634) brought production fully up to origin/main, and it was verified afterwards: /sw.js dxedge-v69, https://dxedge.net/synth/ serving 'Filament - a tube synthesizer - DXEdge', /api/health ok at 04:33:24Z, both standalone shells clean. The reason the earlier caveat was wrong is that deploy.yml's droplet step runs `git fetch origin main` + `git reset --hard origin/main` AND `docker compose restart nginx` UNCONDITIONALLY, with `nginx -t` validating afterwards; backend=false skips only `docker compose build backend` and `docker compose up -d`. Since 69a1385 changed no backend/ file and only tripped the ^nginx/ path regex, the frontend-only branch was sufficient to deploy it completely, nginx carve-out included. SO THE REMAINING QUESTION IS NARROW: why did 69a1385's own run fail or never start, when the pipeline worked 20 minutes later? The distinguishing factor is that 69a1385 took the backend=true branch, so the suspects are `docker compose build backend` (a --no-cache style rebuild), `docker compose up -d`, or the backend-restart verify step that greps `docker compose ps backend` - plus the possibility that the Actions run never started at all. Open the Actions history for 69a1385 and read which step went red. Low urgency, but every future backend or nginx change takes that same branch.

awaiting_james.decision_needed: The /cyber/ page's 'CRITICAL CVEs - LAST 30 DAYS' panel is failing because its NVD query, services.nvd.nist.gov/rest/json/cves/2.0 with cvssV3Severity=CRITICAL plus a 30-day pubStartDate/pubEndDate window, no longer completes inside backend/feedproxy.py's TIMEOUT_S = 15. The proxy returns 504 'upstream feed timed out'. NVD itself is healthy. Not fixable autonomously, and the three options differ in kind: raise TIMEOUT_S, which is a resource limit on an SSRF-sensitive proxy that buffers whole bodies in memory for a 900s TTL, so the same class of change as the MAX_BYTES decision already in your hands; narrow the date window (say 7 days instead of 30), which changes what the panel shows and so changes data semantics; or register an NVD API key, which lifts NVD's rate limits substantially but needs a credential. Needing a credential and changing panel semantics are both named escalation triggers in the brief, and raising a proxy resource limit is the same judgement you already hold on MAX_BYTES.

awaiting_james.detail: The /cyber/ NVD CRITICAL CVEs panel fails, and tonight separated it into TWO independent causes with a controlled comparison. CAUSE 1, the main one: NVD answers the DROPLET a fast 503 while answering an independent client the IDENTICAL query a healthy 200. Measured: droplet through /api/feed, simplified query, 502 'upstream returned 503' at 799ms, 969ms and 851ms, the last after a 75-second quiet window with no probes at all; this container via WebFetch, same query, HTTP 200 with 8 vulnerabilities and totalResults 30863, no rate-limit message. backend/feedproxy.py caches ONLY successes (cache.set sits on the 200 path after a full body read) and the /api/feed nonce never reaches the cache key, which is keyed on the inner url, so those were three real independent refusals and not one cached error. Inference, and NARROWED later the same night (see below): NVD throttles our origin intermittently, plausibly by source IP or by the proxy's self-identifying UA 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; DXEdgeFeedProxy/1.0; +https://dxedge.net)' at feedproxy.py:71. NOT our timeout, NOT the query shape, NOT a general outage. CAUSE 2, independent: the 30-day date-ranged query, which is the shape the page actually sends, also fails from THIS container (SERVER_ERROR then client_error on the permitted retry) and times out at our TIMEOUT_S from the droplet (504 at 15.7s). So that query is genuinely slow or erroring upstream for everyone. Two stacked causes on one panel is why 11-14 and 11-15 produced opposite, convincing, and both wrong shape correlations. THE DECISION, and all four options are outside the autonomous mandate: (a) get a free NVD API key and have feedproxy send it, which lifts the documented unauthenticated rate limit from 5 to 50 requests per 30s and is the option NVD itself recommends, but it is a new credential and needs somewhere to live; (b) change the proxy UA to a plain browser string, a fetch-policy change of the kind the 11-04 flexradio note deliberately put to James rather than making; (c) narrow the date window so the query stops straddling our 15s ceiling, which changes what the panel displays; (d) accept the panel failing and render a quieter placeholder. Worth deciding alongside cisa-advisories-feed-5xx: both are feedproxy fetch-policy questions and answering them one at a time keeps producing nights like this. NARROWED 2026-11-16 AFTER THE POST-DEPLOY LOAD, and this is the current position: the NVD panel SUCCEEDED post-deploy with the dated query from the droplet, about 20 minutes after the three 503s. So this is NOT a hard block and NOT a permanent refusal. The measurements above stand, but the defensible reading is that NVD's behaviour toward the droplet is intermittent and origin-sensitive: bursts of fast upstream 503s to us while an unrelated client is served normally, plus a 30-day dated query slow enough to hit our 15s ceiling. That pattern, intermittent 503s under light load, is the classic signature of unauthenticated per-IP rate limiting, which makes option (a), the free NVD API key, the most likely fix rather than merely one of four. It is still a new credential and still James's call. DO NOT CLOSE THIS on a single clean night: it has now flapped across 11-14, 11-15 and 11-16, and both of the last two runs nearly drew a wrong conclusion from one favourable observation.

awaiting_james.detail: backend/feedproxy.py makes exactly ONE attempt per request and surfaces any failure straight to the page as a dead panel. Three upstreams have now been caught failing a first call and succeeding on an immediate identical retry from the same origin. TONIGHT'S MEASUREMENTS. Google News PQC: page load 502 'upstream returned 429' at 644ms and a .feed-error on screen; the IDENTICAL url then returned 200 with 31,197 bytes at 492ms, and the panel was clean on the second page load. NVD dated CRITICAL query: page load 504 'upstream feed timed out' at 15,834ms against TIMEOUT_S=15; the IDENTICAL url returned 200 in 1,072ms with 64,613 bytes and totalResults 68, and the panel was clean on the second load. EPSS did the same thing on 2026-09-17. Note the proxy caches ONLY successes (cache.set sits on the 200 path after a full body read), so each failure is a real independent refusal and each success is a real fetch, and the two orderings are not a caching artifact. THE DECISION, three options. (1) Add a single bounded retry inside /api/feed on 429, 502, 503 and timeout, with a short backoff of roughly 500ms to 1s and a hard ceiling so one slow upstream cannot pile up workers. Smallest change, kills most of the visible flapping, and it is squarely a backend behavior change, so this run did NOT make it. (2) Leave the proxy alone and have the two pages retry once client side before painting .feed-error. Keeps the backend untouched but has to be done in both standalone HTML files. (3) Accept intermittent blank panels as normal and stop reporting them, in which case say so and these three items can all be closed as working-as-intended. NOT DONE AUTONOMOUSLY because it changes shared backend behavior for every feed on the site, it affects timeout and concurrency characteristics, and the brief says to prefer reporting over guessing on anything less than certain. A retry also slightly changes data semantics by masking real upstream outages, which Step 5 reserves for James.
